stem: After withdrawing the prescribed dose from a single-dose vial for one client, medication remains in the vial. What should the nurse do with the remaining medication?

options.A: Save the remainder for a later dose for the same client if the vial is refrigerated after use.
options.B: Pool the remainder with leftovers from other single-dose vials so a complete dose can be prepared later.
options.C: Use the remainder for another client as long as a new sterile needle and syringe are used.
options.D: Discard the remaining medication; a single-dose vial should not be retained, pooled, or used for another patient.

rationale: CDC safe-injection guidance states that medications from single-dose vials or ampules should not be administered to multiple patients and that leftover contents should not be combined or stored for later use. Current CDC injection-safety guidance also states not to retain excess from a single-dose vial for future use, even for the same patient. Therefore D is correct. A, B, and C each reuse or retain a product intended for single use in ways CDC specifically advises against.
educational_objective: Use single-dose vials for one patient and one procedure/dose episode as intended; discard remaining medication rather than saving, pooling, or sharing leftovers.
source_organization: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC)
source_document_title: Safe Injection Practices to Prevent Transmission of Infections to Patients; Preventing Unsafe Injection Practices
source_version_date: CDC pages dated 2024-04-12 and 2024-03-26; current guidance rechecked 2026-08-17
source_locator: Safe Injection Practices > Recommendations IV.H.4-IV.H.5: use single-dose vials whenever possible; do not use single-dose vials for multiple patients or combine leftover contents; Preventing Unsafe Injection Practices > Basic safe injection practices: do not retain single-dose vial contents for future use, even for the same patient; do not pool leftovers
source_claim_supported: CDC directs that single-dose vials be used for one patient, not shared across patients, and that leftover contents not be pooled or stored for later use; excess single-dose vial contents should not be retained even for later use in the same patient.
blueprint_source_organization: National Council of State Boards of Nursing (NCSBN)
blueprint_locator: Safety and Infection Prevention and Control, printed p.8/PDF p.12: Apply principles of infection prevention (e.g., hand hygiene, aseptic technique, isolation, sterile technique, universal/standard enhanced barrier precautions); Follow procedures for handling biohazardous materials
blueprint_topic: Safety and Infection Prevention and Control — safe injection and medication-vial practices
correction_summary: Replaced the original centralized-pharmacy rationale because the cited secondary ASHP resource did not directly support all claimed centralized-versus-bedside benefits and the construct was weakly nursing-specific. Rebuilt the item as a direct bedside injection-safety decision using current CDC primary guidance on single-dose vials and leftover medication. Key changed from D to D by coincidence, but the clinical construct was fully rewritten.
